summary.en: Risings against Ottoman rule broke out across the Peloponnese and Central Greece in the spring of 1821. The 25th of March, Old Style, is the date the Greek state later chose to commemorate, though the first actions came earlier and in several places at once, including Alexandros Ypsilantis crossing the Pruth into Moldavia in February.

body_html.en:
The revolution had two openings. In the Danubian Principalities, Alexandros Ypsilantis crossed the Pruth from Russian territory on 6 March 1821 at the head of a small force, expecting Russian support that never came. His campaign was over by June.

In the Peloponnese the rising spread through the second half of March, Old Style, from Kalavryta and Patras to the Mani, where Petrobey Mavromichalis and Kolokotronis raised the clans. Within weeks the Ottoman garrisons were shut up in the fortresses and the countryside was in Greek hands. The 25th of March, the feast of the Annunciation, was fixed as the national day in 1838 and is 6 April in the Gregorian calendar used on this map.
